title: Control Chart Monitoring for Detecting Representation Drift Across Fine-Tuning

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear safety chain: detecting when fine-tuning changes safety-relevant mechanisms is directly useful for preventing alignment degradation during fine-tuning. The early warning system has immediate practical application for model developers.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Control charts are conceptually simple (mean +/- sigma bounds). SAELens provides the activation metrics. However, setting up a fine-tuning pipeline and extracting metrics at checkpoints requires moderate engineering skill. Medium compute suffices for small models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires setting up fine-tuning, extracting metrics at checkpoints, computing control limits, and analyzing which components drift. The fine-tuning loop adds engineering overhead. Could be done in 30 hours if using a pre-existing fine-tuning script and a small model.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
